result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A explains why the tour fails in terms of this audience: there are no matters to practise on yet on day one, and these are power users who will resent a tour. It then gives a tight set of in-context learning methods and a three-shortcut fallback for the PM, with no tutorial in the main path. Answer B has strong ideas, including role-aware defaults and usage data to pick the starter set. But it is longer, still includes a short first-run flow, and its claim that lawyers expect a command palette from Westlaw is questionable. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B explains more clearly why a day-one tour fails for these particular users: there are no matters yet, and power users resent being walked through a tour. It also covers every part of item 2, including shortcut hints next to existing actions, the command palette and tips after repeated mouse actions. A's ideas are also strong, but it still keeps a role-aware first-run flow and its pitch to the PM is a bit muddled, while B gives a clearer three-shortcut fallback and test.
